checks.finding: None of the 5 tasks' Scope/Done-When touches the sentinel surfaces (authentication, authorization, payment, PII storage, data migration, externally-visible API contracts): T-001/T-002 add advisory prose to bootstrap/SKILL.md and a ship/SKILL.md human-copy candidate respectively (tasks.md:243-263, :377-400); T-003/T-004 add doc claims to USERGUIDE.md/README.md (tasks.md:509-526, :579-589); T-005 only reads mcp/*/src/server.ts, writing no product file (tasks.md:637-651). design.md:40 states 'No contract change is required or permitted' (no external API touched). T-002's medium tier (tasks.md:379-400) is consistent with policy: its own footprint never opens the live protected ship/SKILL.md for write (guard_invariants.py untouched; BL-004/D-003 verified in Protected Files table tasks.md:176-186), so the task does not itself modify an authorization/access-control mechanism -- the human apply-commit that does touch the protected file is explicitly out of this task's Done-When scope (tasks.md:493-499). No task is high/critical over cosmetic-only scope either. No violation found.

No task in tasks.md carries Risk: high or Risk: critical -- T-001 Risk: medium (tasks.md:243), T-002 Risk: medium (:377), T-003 Risk: medium (:509), T-004 Risk: medium (:579), T-005 Risk: low (:637). The mandatory high/critical Done-When evidence set (Red->Green TDD capture, named independent-reviewer verdict, and for critical a second approver + signed bundle) therefore does not attach to any task in this decomposition; check is vacuously satisfied per risk-gate-matrix.md's tier-conditioned requirements (risk-gate-matrix.md:28-33).

T-001's Done-When (tasks.md:303-367) contains 11 distinct '- [ ]' checkbox items and T-002's Done-When (tasks.md:436-491) contains 10 (grep-verified: 11/10 vs. 5/5/5 for T-003/T-004/T-005), both exceeding the 8-item oversized-task indicator. T-001 alone binds roughly 15 acceptance criteria to one task (AC-001, AC-004-007, AC-008-009, AC-012, AC-027a, AC-027b, AC-017-020, AC-027, plus BL-001 -- see tasks.md:282-286 Requirements line), spanning presence, 4 absence checks, 2 fallback branches, 1 differential run, 2 divergence assertions, 4 open-method runtime items, and 1 regression check, several requiring separately saved verification artifacts (tasks.md:358-363). This concentration in a single task increases the risk that a single implementation/review session partially satisfies the checklist while still being marked 'Implementation Complete', or that the quality gate misses one of the many independently-verifiable properties bundled into one task.

Each functional task has bound error-path/edge-case ACs, not just happy-path: T-001/T-002 carry AC-008/AC-009/AC-010/AC-011 (MCP absent / call-fails fallback, requirements.md:116-126), AC-012/AC-013 (differential outcome-equality edge check, requirements.md:134-140), AC-027a/AC-027b (probe/file divergence branch, requirements.md:148-157), and T-002 additionally AC-026 (protected-file non-write assertion, requirements.md:238-239) -- all cited in tasks.md Requirements lines 282-286 and 416-419. T-003/T-004 (AC-021-024) are guarded by an explicit false-positive/negative check: acceptance-tests.md:140 notes the existing 助言的 usage that makes a bare-keyword check a live false positive, and BL-003 preservation is verified by diff (tasks.md:562, :619). No functional task has only unguarded happy-path criteria.

tasks.md's per-task Test Type fields (T-001: :271-280, T-002: :408-414, T-005: :659-665) faithfully restate acceptance-tests.md's own per-row typing rather than inventing new labels. T-005's registry read across three separate MCP servers is labeled 'unit', consistent with acceptance-tests.md's documented local convention (acceptance-tests.md:164) and design.md Test Strategy point 2 (design.md:177). The dual-runtime rows (AC-017-020) are explicitly disclosed as method-undetermined (OQ-009) rather than mislabeled as a concrete type (tasks.md:353-363, :487-490), matching design.md Risk R-2's warning against a false text-assertion substitute (design.md:209).

No task carries Risk: high or Risk: critical, so the check's mandatory trigger is not present. All 5 tasks nonetheless include explicit Rollback: fields with concrete, scoped revert plans: T-001 tasks.md:290-299 (single-commit prose revert, notes cross-task interaction with T-002), T-002 tasks.md:423-432 (agent-commit revert vs. human-apply-commit revert distinguished), T-003 tasks.md:544-549, T-004 tasks.md:605-609, T-005 tasks.md:671-673 (nothing functional to revert). No gap.

tasks.md Global Constraints (tasks.md:190-197) states 'no two tasks below write the same file' and each task's own Scope/target confirms disjoint file sets: T-001 writes only bootstrap/SKILL.md; T-002 writes only the staged human-copy candidate + MANIFEST.sha256 (never the live protected path, per tasks.md:472-479); T-003 writes only USERGUIDE.md; T-004 writes only README.md; T-005 writes no product file (verification-only, tasks.md:700-702). tests/workflow-documentation.tests.sh is referenced by both T-001 (tasks.md:364-366) and T-004 (tasks.md:620-625), but both instances explicitly require it 'passes unmodified' as a read-only regression check -- neither task edits it, so this is not a write-write overlap.

All 5 tasks declare 'Blockers: None' (tasks.md:288, :421, :542, :603, :669), justified in tasks.md Global Constraints (tasks.md:190-197: 'Task independence, by construction, not by omission... none of the four writable-target tasks... depends on T-002's content') and corroborated by design.md:15 ('They can be implemented in either order and must merge together' -- order-independence, not a hard sequencing dependency) and traceability.md:118-125 ('Task independence, stated plainly... every task above carries Blockers: None'). No task's Scope consumes another task's output artifact, so no missing blocker is evident, and none of the declared 'None' values is spurious since no ordering constraint is asserted.

SKIP: no bugfix or debugging task in scope. All 5 tasks (T-001 add probe to bootstrap, T-002 stage probe for ship, T-003/T-004 add policy prose, T-005 verify existing write-tool absence) are net-new feature, documentation, or preservation-verification work, not remediation of an existing failure -- requirements.md:11 states 'The probe is a genuine create... there is no partial implementation to extend' and REQ-006/T-005 is framed as 'a preservation obligation... satisfied today' (requirements.md:166), not a fix for a broken state.
